title: Copy HDR video and re-encode only the audio
description: A client that plays the HDR video but not its audio (TrueHD, DTS in jellyfin-web) gets the video copied and the audio re-encoded, instead of a full 4K software re-encode with tone mapping.
acceptanceCriteria: HDR10, HLG and DV (with a compatible base layer) copy when the client's profile allows
jellyfin-web plays a 4K HDR film with TrueHD audio from a copy on a 4-core worker without stalls
Tone mapping stays for clients that cannot show HDR

An integration test copies HDR10, HLG, DV 8.1 and DV 7 fixtures through the worker's own ffmpeg path and checks each init segment's sample entry (hvc1, no dvcC/dvvC where the DV layer is dropped) and the master's VIDEO-RANGE
A rolling update cannot break playback: a stream replica serves every copy an api replica of the same or the previous release offers, or docs/running.md states the roll order and a test pins it
source: work queue 6; PRODUCT.md phase3 (HDR direct play and copy not built)
notes: Added after JS-023 (2026-11-08): JS-023 decides DV copies and writes the master, but no test runs a copy through jellyscale's ffmpeg (Jellyfin's arguments drop dvcC, checked by hand only), and its review found that an old replica refuses the HEVC copy a new one offers mid-rollout. Plain HDR copy widens both risks, so they belong here. Built 2026-11-08: CanCopy and canServeCopy accept HDR10, HDR10+ and HLG in HEVC and AV1 (not H.264, not an unscanned range); the master names PQ or HLG, and cdm4 for HDR10+, matching a Jellyfin 12.4 capture (compat/captures/hdr-copy-12.4.md) for 3 films under 6 profiles. A profile that cannot show the range is still tone mapped. An integration test copies HDR10, HLG, DV 8.1 and DV 7 through the worker's own ffmpeg and checks the init segment (hvc1, no dvcC/dvvC, transfer kept). Roll order: stream replicas first (docs/running.md). Measured by the lead: a 4K HDR10 HEVC film with 5.1 TrueHD copies at about 73x real time on 4 CPUs (30 s in 0.41 s). Backlog: no automated check of a 4K TrueHD copy; the e2e copy scenario needs E2E_HEVC=1 so it never runs in CI (CI's Chrome plays AV1, so an AV1 HDR10 copy scenario could); no ffmpeg-path test of an AV1 HDR copy; the DV 7 fixture has no enhancement-layer NALs; the roll-order check pins wording; the capture note's TrueHD observation is not in its JSON.
